patch_description:
The previous program failed validation for multiple structural reasons: (1) it returned an empty `column_orderings` list `[]`, giving the evaluator no valid per-row column orderings; (2) `column_recursion` inserted rows via `result_df.loc[i]` from `as_completed` futures, scrambling row order and writing into an empty DataFrame with no rows; (3) the recursive path mutated/dropped columns (`original_index` handling, group `.iloc` writes) and its final shape/value assertions could not hold, so rows and cells were effectively lost or altered; (4) `find_max_group_value` mixed pandas/Counter hashing with `getattr` attribute lookups on named tuples that don't match real column names. In short, the algorithm did not preserve data or produce consistent per-row permutations.

The fix replaces the whole editable block with a correct, bounded construction-selection algorithm aligned with the true objective (character-Trie reuse measured by sorted-string adjacent LCP sums): serialize every cell exactly (missing -> "", others -> str), factorize columns once into integer codes and value lengths, build three cheap candidate row-field orderings — (A) a global frequency-ranked column order using sum(len(v)*cnt*(cnt-1)), (B) a recursive conditional prefix partition tree picking per-group columns by length-weighted pair repetition and permuting only within groups, and (C) a variant using immediate (cnt-1) savings — then score each candidate's serialized rows with the deterministic ideal Trie objective (sorted strings, adjacent LCP via C-speed slice-equality binary search) and output the best. Every original cell value and row is preserved (values copied verbatim into object-dtype rows), each row gets a valid column-ordering list consistent with the returned data, `col_merge` reuses the parent `merging_columns` when available, and the public `reorder` signature is unchanged.
